root.label: RAII & Resource Safety
root.note: Binding resource invariants to object lifetimes guarantees deterministic cleanup across every exit path.

children.label: Core Principle
children.note: Constructors establish resource invariants and destructors release them at lexical scope exit.

children.label: Invariant Acquisition
children.note: A successfully constructed RAII object always holds either a valid resource or a safe empty state.

children.label: Scope-Exit Release
children.note: Cleanup fires uniformly on fallthrough, early return, break, and exception unwinding.

children.label: Non-Memory Resources
children.note: RAII manages file descriptors, mutexes, sockets, transactions, and temporary state guards alike.

children.label: Destruction Rules
children.note: C++ prescribes strict reverse teardown ordering and implicit noexcept on destructors.

children.label: Reverse Order
children.note: Locals, members, and bases are destroyed in exact reverse order of construction completion.

children.label: Implicit noexcept
children.note: Destructors are implicitly noexcept(true) since C++11 unless explicitly overridden or inheriting throwing ones.

children.label: std::terminate Trap
children.note: Allowing an exception to escape a noexcept destructor immediately calls std::terminate.

children.label: Exception Unwinding
children.note: Exceptions unwind only completely constructed objects and subobjects.

children.label: Completed Subobjects
children.note: Every base or member whose constructor finished before a throw is destroyed automatically.

children.label: No Partial Destructor
children.note: When a class constructor throws, that class's own destructor never runs because lifetime never began.

children.label: No Abrupt Exit Unwind
children.note: Calling std::exit or std::abort bypasses automatic stack frame destructors.

children.label: Special Members
children.note: Ownership design separates zero-boilerplate composition from custom resource handles.

children.label: Rule of Zero
children.note: Domain classes hold standard RAII members and declare zero custom special member functions.

children.label: Rule of Five
children.note: Low-level resource wrappers declaring a destructor must explicitly define or delete copy and move operations.

children.label: Suppressed Moves
children.note: Any user-declared destructor—even = default—suppresses compiler-generated move operations.

children.label: std::exchange Moves
children.note: Transfer handles cleanly with std::exchange(other.handle, invalid) and mark moves noexcept.

children.label: Standard Vocabulary
children.note: Standard library smart pointers and lock guards encode ownership contracts directly in types.

children.label: unique_ptr Deleters
children.note: Stateless functor deleters preserve single-pointer size whereas function-pointer deleters add storage overhead.

children.label: shared_ptr & weak_ptr
children.note: Use shared ownership sparingly with make_shared and break reference cycles with weak_ptr.

children.label: scoped_lock Guards
children.note: Acquire multiple mutexes atomically without deadlock and release them automatically at scope exit.
